title: Kerala Nature Itinerary: Hills, Forests, Waterfalls and Backwaters
seoTitle: Kerala Nature Itinerary: Falls, Hills and Backwaters | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: A seven-day Kerala nature itinerary from Kochi: Athirappilly Falls, Munnar and Eravikulam, Thekkady's Periyar lake and the backwaters at Kumarakom.
description: A seven-day nature itinerary for Kerala from Kochi: Athirappilly and Vazhachal falls, two days in Munnar with Eravikulam's grasslands and tea country, Thekkady with Periyar lake and forest walks, and the Vembanad backwaters at Kumarakom or Alappuzha, with drive times, seasons and variations for Wayanad and Vagamon.
dek: In a week, Kerala takes you from waterfalls to tea hills, forest lakes and palm-lined backwaters.

hero.alt: A boat on the backwaters at Kumarakom, Kerala

intro: This loop starts and ends in Kochi, which has an international airport and good rail links. It climbs from the plains to the Western Ghats and back down to the backwaters, with no drive longer than about five hours.
It suits families and first-time visitors, with short walks, boat rides and comfortable stays throughout.
quickAnswer: A good seven-day Kerala nature itinerary runs Kochi to Athirappilly Falls (day 1), on to Munnar (day 2), a full day in Munnar with Eravikulam and tea country (day 3), Munnar to Thekkady (day 4), Periyar lake and forest walks (day 5), Thekkady to the Kumarakom backwaters (day 6), and back to Kochi (day 7). October to March is best; the falls are fullest in the monsoon.
takeaways: Kochi is the natural start and end point.
Book the Periyar lake boat and Eravikulam entry early in peak season.
Eravikulam closes for a few weeks early in the year for Nilgiri tahr calving.
A one-night houseboat or a lakeside stay both work for the backwaters.
Allow extra time for hill roads in the monsoon.

sections.heading: Day 1: Athirappilly
paras: Drive about two hours from Kochi to Athirappilly on the Chalakudy river. Walk to the viewpoint and down towards the base of the falls, then visit Vazhachal a few kilometres upstream.

sections.heading: Days 2 and 3: Munnar
paras: The drive from Athirappilly to Munnar takes about four to five hours as the road climbs into the tea hills. Spend the next day at Eravikulam National Park, where a park bus takes you into the grasslands and Nilgiri tahr are often seen, then visit the tea museum and Mattupetty dam.

sections.heading: Days 4 and 5: Thekkady
paras: Drive about three to four hours through cardamom and spice country to Thekkady. The next morning, take the forest department's boat on Periyar lake and join a guided nature walk. Spice garden visits are an easy afternoon option.

sections.heading: Days 6 and 7: The backwaters
paras: Drive about four hours down to Kumarakom on Vembanad lake. Stay by the lake or on a one-night houseboat. On the last morning, walk in the Kumarakom bird sanctuary at dawn before driving about two hours to Kochi.

sections.heading: Variations
list: Add Wayanad for forests and Chembra peak (two to three days, from Kozhikode).
Swap Kumarakom for Munroe Island for quieter canals.
Add Vagamon's meadows between Thekkady and Kumarakom.

sections.heading: Getting around
paras: Hire a car with a driver from Kochi for the whole loop; hill roads to Munnar and Thekkady are narrow and winding, and drivers know where to stop for viewpoints and tea. KSRTC buses link all the stops if you are on a budget, but they add time. Book the Eravikulam entry and the Periyar lake boat online where possible, especially on weekends and in the Christmas holidays.

If you have only five days, drop Athirappilly and drive straight from Kochi to Munnar, then continue to Thekkady and Kumarakom. With ten days, add Wayanad in the north or Vagamon and Munroe Island in the south.

sections.heading: When to go
paras: October to March is best for clear views and comfortable walks. From June to September the waterfalls are at their fullest and the hills very green, but roads can slip and some viewpoints close. April and May are hot on the coast but pleasant in Munnar.

safety: Stay on marked trails and viewpoints, and heed local closures after heavy rain.
Permits, entry rules, seasonal closures and timings change; check official sources before you go.
Carry your waste back, avoid loud music and never feed wildlife.
Drive times are approximate and depend on traffic, weather and road works.
Do not swim near waterfalls or in rivers; currents are strong.
packing: Light cotton clothes and a warm layer for Munnar

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Kerala's nature?
faqs.a: Seven days covers Athirappilly, Munnar, Thekkady and the backwaters; add three for Wayanad.

faqs.q: Is this itinerary good for families?
faqs.a: Yes. The walks are short and the boat rides easy.

faqs.q: Should I choose a houseboat or a lakeside stay?
faqs.a: A one-night houseboat is a classic experience; a lakeside stay is more flexible.
Usually for a few weeks early in the year for the Nilgiri tahr calving season; check before booking.

faqs.q: Can I do this trip in the monsoon?
faqs.a: Yes, for waterfalls and green hills, but allow extra time for hill roads.
Kochi, which also has good rail connections.
